guides.title: Email security guides
guides.subtitle: Understand SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to protect your domain against email spoofing and phishing.
guides.ctaSubtitle: Test your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configuration in one click. Our tool analyzes your domain and tells you exactly what to fix.
guides.spfDescription: SPF defines which servers are authorized to send emails for your domain. It's the first line of defense against email address spoofing.
guides.dkimDescription: DKIM uses asymmetric cryptography to sign your emails. It ensures the content hasn't been modified in transit and that the email actually comes from your domain.
guides.dmarcDescription: DMARC orchestrates SPF and DKIM by defining a clear policy for emails that fail verification. It also adds a reporting system to monitor your domain.

dns.spf_softfail: SPF in softfail (~all) — unauthorized emails are not rejected
dns.spf_neutral: SPF in neutral mode (?all) — no protection
dns.spf_pass_all: SPF with +all — DANGER: allows anyone to send
dns.dmarc_none: DMARC in monitoring mode (p=none) — does not block spoofing
dns.dmarc_quarantine: DMARC in quarantine — spoofed emails go to spam but are not rejected
dns.dmarc_no_reporting: No DMARC reporting configured (rua=) — you won't see spoofing attempts
dns.rec_add_dmarc: Add a DMARC record: _dmarc.yourdomain TXT "v=DMARC1; p=reject; adkim=s; aspf=s; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain"
dns.rec_dmarc_none_to_reject: Change your DMARC policy from p=none to p=reject to block spoofing
dns.rec_dmarc_quarantine_to_reject: Upgrade your DMARC policy from p=quarantine to p=reject for full blocking
dns.rec_add_rua: Add rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain to your DMARC to receive reports
dns.rec_add_spf: Add an SPF record: yourdomain TXT "v=spf1 include:yourprovider -all"
dns.rec_harden_spf: Harden your SPF by replacing ~all with -all (hardfail)
dns.rec_add_dkim: Enable DKIM in your email provider and add the public key to your DNS zone

faq.question: What is email spoofing?
faq.answer: Email spoofing is an identity theft technique where someone sends an email pretending to be someone else. The attacker forges the sender address so the message appears to come from a legitimate source, like your company or a colleague. It's one of the most common methods used in phishing attacks.

faq.question: How do I know if my domain is vulnerable?
faq.answer: Use our free tool: simply enter your domain name in the search bar above. SpoofCheck automatically analyzes your DNS records (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and tells you if your domain is protected against email spoofing.

faq.question: What are SPF, DKIM, and DMARC?
faq.answer: SPF (Sender Policy Framework) defines which servers are authorized to send emails for your domain. DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) adds a cryptographic signature to your emails to ensure their integrity. DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) combines SPF and DKIM and defines what to do when authentication fails.

faq.question: How do I fix an email vulnerability?
faq.answer: To protect your domain, you need to properly configure three DNS records: an SPF record listing your authorized sending servers, DKIM keys for signing your emails, and a DMARC policy telling receiving servers how to handle unauthenticated emails.

faq.question: Is this test free?
faq.answer: Yes, SpoofCheck is 100% free. You can check as many domains as you want, with no signup or limits. DNS checks are public and non-intrusive.
